MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
December 2, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on
Monday, December 2, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300
Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Waronek led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were
COUNCILMEMBERS: Gazeley, Traina, Waronek, Sanchez, and Mayor Savidan. Also
present were City Manager Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin,
Community Services Director McPherron, Parks and Recreation Director Harding,
Public Works Director Damasse, Administrative Services Director Chavez, and Assistant
City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda.  Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

3. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, spoke about ADA access at one of the medical offices in
Lomita. Mr. McGrath asked for clarification on how a recent water bill adjustment was
calculated. Also, Mr. McGrath asked that City Council revisit the process of how items
are placed on the agenda. Furthermore, Mr. McGrath stated he was opposed to using
taxpayer money for the purchase of an iPad for one of the Councilmembers. Lastly, Mr.
McGrath suggested that staff look into cheaper options for the purchase of a lawn
mower.

  Page 1
 George Kivett, Lomita resident, congratulated the newly elected Councilmembers,
Mayor, and Mayor Pro Tem. Mr. Kivett spoke about the appeal process of Planning
Commission decisions, and asked Council to consider reducing the period of time
associated with the appeal process. Also, Mr. Kivett stated that the crosswalk at
Narbonne Avenue is still not working. Lastly, Mr. Kivett congratulated Scott Gobble on
his retirement from Southern California Edison.

Scott Gobble, Retired Regional Manager for Southern California Edison, introduced
Southern California Edison’s Interim Regional Manager, Ron Garcia, whom in turn
stated that he was honored to represent the City of Lomita. Councilmembers Savidan,
Waronek, and Gazeley congratulated Mr. Gobble on his retirement, and thanked him for
all his service to the City.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE
CITY COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina asked that staff look into the ADA compliance issue at the
medical office, which Mr. McGrath spoke about. Councilmember Traina also asked that
Chris Dunn be invited again to a City Council meeting for recognition of winning first
place at the Giant Pumpkin Weigh-Off & Contest at the 2013 Pumpkinmania at Tanaka
Farms, as he was unable to attend the Council meeting on November 18, 2013.
Furthermore, Councilmember Traina requested a future agenda item to discuss the
possibility of inviting the community’s religious leaders to lead Council’s invocation.
Councilmembers Sanchez and Waronek agreed to placing the discussion item on a
future agenda. Lastly, Councilmember Traina requested that a two-member City
Council subcommittee be established to review and come up with creative ways for
fixing City streets, and that another subcommittee be created for the City’s upcoming
50th Anniversary. Councilmembers Sanchez and Waronek agreed to placing these
requested items on a future agenda.

Councilmember Waronek announced that sign-ups have started for the 2014 Lomita
Little League.

Councilmember Sanchez requested a future agenda item to discuss reconvening the
General Plan Advisory Committee. Councilmembers Waronek and Traina agreed to
placing the discussion item on a future agenda.

Councilmember Gazeley reported that he attended both the South Bay Cities Council of
Government (SBCCOG) and the Southern California Association of Governments
(SCAG) meetings and on November 25, 2013 State of the Region 2013 meeting.
Councilmember Gazeley invited all Councilmembers and the City Manager to attend the

  Page 2
 upcoming SBCCOG workshop on January 9, 2014. Furthermore, Councilmember
Gazeley requested a future agenda item for considering a different day and time for City
Council meetings. Councilmember Sanchez and Mayor Savidan agreed to placing the
discussion item on a future agenda.

Mayor Savidan reported that he attended the Kiwanis Club meeting honoring senior
citizens.

5. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock reported that a water leak on Eshelman Avenue had been repaired,
and that the leak was not related to the Eshelman Avenue Waterline Replacement and
Resurfacing Project. According to City Manager Rock, the paving of Eshelman Avenue
should be completed shortly.

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that the crosswalk at Narbonne
Avenue is currently not operational, and that inlaid pavement would not work and would
fail again. Therefore, City Manager Rock stated that alternative technology for the
crosswalk will be presented to the Public Safety and Traffic Commission for
consideration.

Lastly, City Manager Rock reported that a water rate study will be conducted in the near
future, and based on a comparison with surrounding jurisdictions water rates in Lomita
are in the lower third compared to those in the South Bay.

6. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Traina requested that Items 6.C, 6.D, and 6.M be pulled from the
Consent Agenda for discussion.

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember
Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried unanimously, minus Items 6.C, 6.D and
6.M.

Item 6.C – Referring to vouchers #511719, #511677, and #511678, Councilmember
Traina stated that staff should consider using Lomita businesses wherever possible,
especially when similar businesses are located here in Lomita. In regards to voucher
#511657 (purchase of an iPad for a Councilmember), Councilmember Traina stated that
he does not support those types of purchases, as taxpayers’ money should not be used
for such expenses.

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve Item 6.C. Councilmember Traina seconded

  Page 3
 the motion, but opposed the approval of voucher #511657.  The motion carried
unanimously.

Item 6.D - In response to Councilmember Traina’s question regarding open employment
positions, Administrative Services Director Chavez stated that current recruitments are
for currently vacant positions that have been budgeted for 2013-2014. Councilmember
Traina moved to approve Item 6.D. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion,
which carried unanimously.

Item 6.M – Councilmember Traina stated that according to his research, there are other
companies and options that are cheaper than the recommended option for the lawn
mower purchase, and recommended that staff should explore other options. Discussion
followed regarding the proposed option and specifications of the Toro lawn mower,
including fuel, the warranty, and compliance with the Clean Air Act. Parks Field
Operations Manager Sansbury, stated that staff’s recommendation is to stay with the
same brand of lawn mower, as it is reliable, and that the proposed lawn mower has
already been tested and performs very well. Councilmember Gazeley made a motion to
approve the purchase of the lawn mower as recommended by staff. Councilmember
Waronek seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

7. INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE – ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2013-09
  REGARDING VERTICAL CLEARANCE FOR COMMERCIAL PARKING
  GARAGES

According to Assistant City Manager Sugano, staff has conducted research on vertical
clearance requirements for commercial parking garages, including the surveying of
other cities, and King’s Way Church on 251st Street is requesting an amendment to
reduce the vertical clearance from nine feet (9’), to eight feet and two inches (8’2”).
Assistant City Manager Sugano noted that the proposed reduction in vertical clearance
in commercial parking garages has been reviewed and recommended for approval by
the Planning Commission.

Councilmember Sanchez stated that he had reviewed the Los Angeles County
Commercial Accessibility Plan Review List, which states that owners are responsible for
compliance with the most current ADA and HUD regulations, and according to the
Commercial Accessibility Review List, 114 inches are required for vertical clearance in

  Page 5
 commercial parking garages. Therefore, Councilmember Sanchez stated that he
agreed with the proposed amendment to reduce vertical clearance from 9’ to 8’2’ in
commercial parking garages, but wanted to make sure that a reference to ADA and
HUD requirements is included in the Lomita Municipal Code.

Discussion followed regarding the allowable vertical clearance for regular commercial
garages and the ADA requirement of 114”.

Mayor Savidan opened the Public Hearing.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, spoke in favor of approving the proposed ordinance.

Nori Hana, Applicant and Representative of King's Way Church, stated that dedicated
handicap parking spaces are already in place, and that the amendment was being
requested for a regular parking garage.

Mayor Savidan closed the Public Hearing.

City Attorney Hogin clarified that since the ADA and HUD reference was not included in
the proposed ordinance, two separate actions would be required to approve the
requested amendment, and that staff would need to bring back a separate ordinance
incorporating the ADA and HUD requirements by reference. Councilmember Sanchez
moved to introduce on the first reading an amendment to the Lomita Municipal Code
amending Section 11-1.66.08, reducing the minimum vertical clearance of commercial
parking garages from 9’ to 8’2”. Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion, which
carried unanimously.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to direct staff to bring back a suggestion on the
feasibility of integrating the ADA and HUD requirements into the Lomita Municipal Code
by reference. Councilmembers Gazeley, Waronek, and Mayor Savidan agreed to place
the proposed item on a future agenda.

  SCHEDULED ITEMS:

8. COPS PROGRAM FUNDING ALLOCATION

Community Services Director McPherron stated that the City receives $100,000
annually for the CORE Program for public safety. According to Director McPherron, this
allocation will go toward front staff policing services, for the Community Resource
Deputy or the CORE Deputy. Councilmember Traina moved to accept the $100,000 for
the CORE Program. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried
unanimously.

  Page 6
 9. STREET SWEEPING ON CUL-DE-SAC STREETS

Community Services Director McPherron reviewed the procedure for posting street
sweeping signs on City streets, including cul-de-sacs, and explained that any resident
could request that street sweeping signs be posted, stated that such requests are
reviewed by the Traffic Advisory Committee. According to Director McPherron, the past
practice of putting up street sweeping signs required obtaining input from residents,
which getting a consensus was difficult to do, but now staff sends out notification letters
to affected residents and invites them to voice their opinion during a meeting of the
Technical Traffic Advisory Committee when that specific item is discussed. Director
McPherron noted that before street sweeping enforcement begins, a grace period is
provided.

Bill Boyer, Lomita resident, suggested that City Council change the current practice, and
revert back to the old practice of requiring the consent of a majority of residents in order
for street sweeping signs to be posted.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to receive and file the staff report. Mayor Savidan
seconded the motion.

Discussion followed on the fact that not all streets have street sweeping signs posted,
and whether weekly street sweeping is even necessary. Director McPherron noted that
a resolution passed in 2007 regulates the process and requires that street sweeping
signs be posted on all City streets.

Mayor Savidan stated that there was a consensus among the Council to bring this item
back for discussion. The original motion was amended to direct staff to bring this item
back to Council for discussion. The motion carried unanimously.

10. SELECTING A DATE AND TIME FOR THE CITY COUNCIL STRATEGIC
  PLANNING WORKSHOP

Councilmembers agreed to Wednesday, March 5, 2014, as the date for the 2ND Annual
City Council Strategic Planning Workshop, with a start time of 4 p.m.

11. POSSIBLE CANCELLATION OF DECEMBER 16, 2013 CITY COUNCIL MEETING

City Manager Rock recommended cancelling the City Council meeting schedule for
December 16, 2013, and clarified that the accounts payable process will continue
uninterrupted as the Administrative Services Director approves all demands, while
Council only audits the demands. City Attorney Hogin added that it is normal for
jurisdictions to go dark during the second meeting in December.

  Page 7
 Joe McGrath, Cindy Segawa, and George Kivett, Lomita residents, opposed cancelling
the second meeting in December 2013.

Bill Boyer, Lomita resident, suggested cancelling the Council meeting, but that the
amount per meeting should be deducted from Councilmembers’ paychecks.

Councilmember Gazeley moved to cancel the second City Council meeting in
December 2013. Councilmember Savidan seconded the motion, which passed 3-2 by
the following roll call vote:

  AYES: Councilmembers Waronek, Gazeley, and Mayor Savidan.

  NOES: Councilmembers Traina and Sanchez.

12. ORGANIZATIONAL ASSIGNMENTS FOR COUNCILMEMBERS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, asked why the Public Finance Authority was not included
on the list of City Council assignments, to which City Manager Rock responded that the
Public Finance Authority was created for the water bond, and is not a Council
assignment.
